title: Pareto-front explorer: quant tradeoff lab notes
body:
Purpose: quick lab worksheet and decision aid to build a Pareto-front based quantization selector for workloads. The idea is to move beyond single-point heuristics (+/− fixed dB thresholds) and produce a small set of candidate quant profiles that sit on the empirical cost-quality-latency Pareto frontier for a given workload (prompt mix + SLOs).

Scope and deliverables:
- Single-sheet simulator that consumes per-profile microbenchmarks and per-workload fidelity deltas, then computes Pareto-efficient buckets.
- Output: ranked candidate profiles with recommended fallback/rollout policy and a short rationale string.
- Guidance section with tuning knobs for latency SLOs, cost headroom, and acceptable quality regressions.

Data model (columns we expect to populate):
- profile_id: short label (e.g., int8-static, fp8-mixed, 4bit-kvcache)
- hw_class: e.g., A100-40GB, H100-80GB, t4-like (for cost normalization)
- cost_per_token_usd: measured on-host cost (includes amortized infra + infra fee)
- cycle_latency_ms_p50: median token latency microbenchmark (tokens after prefix)
- cycle_latency_ms_p95: 95th percentile latency
- quality_delta_pct: relative decrease in task metric vs FP16 baseline (positive means worse)
- example_workload_qps: expected QPS for workload profile (user input)
- effective_throughput_toks_per_sec: derived metric from hw + batch config
- cache_savings_pct: expected KV/prefix cache hit rate for this workload
- notes: short text field for experiment specifics (seed, prompt set, temp)

How to measure (recommended minimal protocol):
1) Microbench each profile on target hardware using our benchmark harness (bench/quantbench). Record p50/p95 for tokens 1..N across typical sequence lengths.
2) Run a small eval set (200–1000 examples representative of workload) to compute quality_delta_pct (e.g., exact-match, BLEU, F1, or custom metric). Include statistical variance.
3) Run workload replay (or synthetic mix) to estimate cache_savings_pct and effective_throughput.
4) Compute cost_per_token_usd by combining cloud rate card, GPU utilization from bench, and operational markup. Store in sheet as a single normalized number.

Core formulas (text for spreadsheet implementation):
- adjusted_token_cost = cost_per_token_usd * (1 - cache_savings_pct)
- latency_score = cycle_latency_ms_p95 (or weighted: 0.6*p95 + 0.4*p50 depending on SLO)
- quality_penalty = max(0, quality_delta_pct)  // treat improvements as zero penalty
- utility = w_cost*(normalized_cost) + w_latency*(normalized_latency) + w_quality*(normalized_quality_penalty)
  - normalized_cost = (adjusted_token_cost - min_cost) / (max_cost - min_cost)
  - normalized_latency = (latency_score - min_latency) / (max_latency - min_latency)
  - normalized_quality_penalty = (quality_penalty - min_q) / (max_q - min_q)
- Pareto flag: a profile is Pareto-efficient if no other profile has lower-or-equal cost, lower-or-equal latency_score and strictly lower quality_penalty (or better in at least one). Implement via pairwise comparisons; mark boolean column.

Usability knobs (inputs to expose to PM/SE/Customer):
- SLO target (ms p95): filter out profiles with p95 > SLO + guard_band_ms (guard default: 10% of SLO)
- Max acceptable quality drop (%): user-set cap; filter out profiles with quality_delta_pct > cap
- Cost preference slider: weights w_cost/w_latency/w_quality (default: 0.5/0.3/0.2) for utility ranking
- Rollout aggressiveness: how many profiles to surface (1..5) and whether to recommend canary percentile size.

Example walkthrough (toy numbers):
- Inputs: workload QPS: 25, SLO p95=120ms, max_quality_drop=3%
- Profiles measured:
  - fp16-baseline: cost 0.0032, p95 95ms, q_drop 0%
  - fp8-mixed: cost 0.0019, p95 105ms, q_drop 0.9%
  - int8-static: cost 0.0011, p95 140ms, q_drop 1.8%
  - 4bit-kvsplit: cost 0.0007, p95 210ms, q_drop 4.5%
- Applying SLO filter (p95 <= 132ms with 10% guard): candidates = fp16-baseline, fp8-mixed (int8-static excluded due to p95)
- Pareto frontier among candidates = {fp16-baseline, fp8-mixed} because fp8 reduces cost and has small quality penalty but slightly higher latency.
- Recommendation: surface fp8-mixed as primary cost-saving candidate with a 10% canary and automatic rollback to fp16 if error rate or latency p95 regresses >10% vs baseline.

Decision policy heuristics (recommended defaults to encode in model):
- If SLO is tight (p95 target < 50ms), prefer profiles with <5% increase in p95 vs baseline. Rank primarily by latency.
- If throughput-led (high QPS where unit cost dominates), allow up to 5% quality drop for >30% cost savings.
- If workload has high cache_savings_pct (>40%), prefer lower-precision profiles since effective cost will be lower and latency amortized.
- When quality_delta_pct has high variance across prompts, bias towards higher-precision profiles unless user can define per-prompt exceptions.

Rollout template (short):
1) Canary: 5–10% traffic to selected quant profile for N=24h or until 100k tokens served. Metrics: p95 latency, error rate, business metric.
2) Evaluate: if latency or errors exceed thresholds, pause and revert. If quality regression measured on live prompts (via eval hooks) > allowed cap, revert.
3) Graduated ramp: 10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% with automated checks at each stage.

Analyses to run (experiments to prioritize):
- Per-prompt sensitivity sweep: find prompts that are brittle to 4-bit and flag them as exclusion patterns for aggressive quantization.
- Batch-size vs latency trade sweep for each hw_class: sometimes increasing batch slightly reduces cost without blowing p95.
- Cache-aware experiments: measure end-to-end per-session token counts to estimate real cache_savings_pct; upstream caching policies can change the math.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide canonical cost normalization scheme across cloud regions (list of region multipliers).
- Create small library of standardized eval sets by vertical (search chat, summary, code generation) so quality deltas are comparable across customers.
- Add support for mixed-precision inference (per-layer policy) and represent it in profile_id semantics.
- Integrate with rollout automation (Console API) to export recommended policy JSON: {profile, canary_size, metric_checks, rollback_policy}.

Appendix: quick checklist for running this sheet in a new customer engagement
- Collect baseline fp16 runs: bench + eval set + replay logs
- Run candidate quant profiles with identical seeds and batch configs
- Populate sheet columns and verify min/max normalizers are computed from current candidate set
- Run pareto filter, inspect flagged candidates, and annotate notes column with hypothesis and confidence level
- Pick 1–2 candidates for canary and schedule rollout with SE

Contact: Asha Rao (owner) — ping in #optimize or DM for clarifications.
